name: ModForge
author: neostryder
description:
Make your own mod from inside the game. Start from something that already exists, such as a monster, a sword, a shop or a spell, and the workshop shows you what it is made of, how each of its numbers compares with similar things in the game, and what you would need to change to get the thing you have in mind. When you are happy with it, one button forges the mod, loads it for this session and reloads the game so you are playing it. You can also save it as a file to give to someone else.

You do not have to know JSON to use it. If you want to see it, every screen can show you the exact file it is about to write, and a mod it built can be taken away, edited by hand and brought back.

The workshop tab appears in the corner of the screen. Tap it to open the workshop.

rules.title: Show the workshop tab
rules.description: Puts a small tab in the corner of the main screen. Tapping it opens the workshop. On by default, since the tab is the only way to open the workshop.

rules.title: Remember work in progress
rules.description: Keeps unfinished mods between sessions, in this install's own settings rather than in any character's save. With this off, the workshop starts empty every time and the only way to keep something is to finish it. On by default. The storage it uses can run out of room without reporting it, so only a finished mod is certain to be kept.

rules.title: Let me test what I built, in the game
rules.description: Adds a Test panel that uses the game's own debug commands to set things up around the thing you just made: put one in front of you, take you to the depth it belongs at, make you the level it is balanced for, give you the gold a shop would want for it, and map the level so you can find it. Off by default because none of the panel's controls work until the panel has stopped this session from being saved, and that cannot be undone. Your character on disk keeps whatever their last save held and nothing after that is written, so testing cannot spoil a character you are keeping, but anything you do in a test session is lost. The panel names the character and explains all of this before the button that turns saving off.
